false_outliers.summary: backend: HTTP handlers in common/** call response.Response()
false_outliers.reason: 3 of 4 outliers return a Response through helpers (SecurityAuditLogListView via paginator.get_paginated_response; OrgUpdateView put/patch via _write, which returns Response), and AttachmentDownloadView legitimately streams a FileResponse.

false_outliers.summary: backend: HTTP handlers in cases/** call response.Response()
false_outliers.reason: Every outlier returns a Response through a helper: CaseKanbanView.get via _get_status_kanban/_get_pipeline_kanban (return Response), SolutionDetailView put/patch via _update, SolutionListView via get_paginated_response, and the time views via create_entry/start_timer, which return Response.

false_outliers.summary: backend: HTTP handlers in leads/** call response.Response()
false_outliers.reason: Both outliers return a Response through helpers: LeadIntakePostView.post via _answer/_refuse/_refused (_answer is `return Response(body, status=code)`), LeadKanbanView.get via _get_status_kanban/_get_pipeline_kanban, which return Response.

Both outliers in window_state.py read Redis through get_anchor_timestamp/get_current_window/_floored, which call get_redis_client() themselves, so they comply through a helper; members like record_timed_out_entry (retry_state.py) and mark_type_triggered (type_tracking.py) call it directly.

get_window_date_range and get_window_date_range_for_index build keys through get_anchor_timestamp/get_current_window/_floored, which call _get_key(); only update_window_cell hand-builds its matrix key with an f-string (same pattern persist_window_results and get_backfill_status use), so 2 of 3 outliers are not_violation.

false_outliers.summary: HTTP handlers in backend/** (actions files) pass `content` to responses.JSONResponse()
false_outliers.reason: All three outliers in teams/actions.py do pass the content, positionally (JSONResponse({...}, status_code=...)), while members in projects/actions.py and notifications/actions.py use content=; the tool only saw the keyword. Hesitated with ACCEPT if the rule is read strictly as 'use the content= keyword', which would be a minor style look.

incidental.summary: exported values in saleor/core/** do not read os.environ directly
incidental.reason: Members (auth.py AUTH_HEADER_PREFIXES, jwt.py JWT_* names, db/connection.py TRACEBACK_LIMIT) are fixed literals with no need for configuration; the one outlier, DEFAULT_CURRENCY in the dev-only random_data.py, is the one value that is configurable and mirrors the same os.environ.get('DEFAULT_CURRENCY','USD') in giftcard/models.py, while core/views.py and cleaners/html.py read os.getenv directly too, so no team choice against direct env reads is visible. Hesitated with ACCEPT (routing config through settings.py would be cleaner).

incidental.summary: backend: functions in app/services/providers/garmin/** call str()
incidental.reason: Members call str() only to normalise a `str | UUID` user_id (e.g. `uid = str(user_id)` in retry_state.py, type_tracking.py); the outliers pass user_id straight to helpers (_get_key, get_anchor_timestamp) that do the conversion, so they lack the need. Either incidental or false_outliers via R6; WRONG either way.

incidental.summary: HTTP handlers in backend/** (actions files) are wrapped in get_db()
incidental.reason: Handlers take Depends(get_db) because they query the database (tasks/actions.py, notifications/actions.py); intersecting_tiles in projects/actions.py only runs GridService.trim_grid_to_aoi on the body and needs no connection, so a DB-free handler would be flagged for nothing.

incidental.summary: HTTP handlers in app/dashboard/** call redirect()
incidental.reason: Handlers redirect after POST actions or failed checks (api_key.py, coupon.py, app.py); the outliers are GET-only pages or a CSV download (alias_export.py) with no action to redirect after.

incidental.summary: HTTP handlers in app/dashboard/** call url_for()
incidental.reason: url_for() is called because handlers redirect to named routes (api_key.py, coupon.py); the outliers build no URLs: read-only renders, a CSV download, and app.py which redirects to request.url, a pattern also used in api_key.py:60.

incidental.summary: HTTP handlers in app/dashboard/** call flash()
incidental.reason: flash() is called by handlers that report the result of an action (api_key.py, coupon.py); the outliers return a CSV (alias_export.py), render read-only pages (notification.py, pricing.py, refused_email.py) or just set a cookie (setup_done.py), so they lack the need.

incidental.summary: HTTP handlers in app/dashboard/** call flash() before redirect()
incidental.reason: The order is a by-product of early returns: enter_admin.py:30 and enter_sudo.py:48 redirect on success paths that need no message before a later error flash, and setup_done.py only sets a cookie and redirects with nothing to flash; none is a mistake.

incidental.summary: HTTP handlers in app/dashboard/** call flash() before render_template()
incidental.reason: Handlers flash before render_template only when they process a form and have a message (api_key.py, coupon.py); notifications_route, subscription_success and refused_email_route are read-only pages with nothing to flash.

incidental.summary: HTTP handlers in app/auth/** call redirect() before url_for()
incidental.reason: redirect() appearing before url_for() is just the nesting redirect(url_for(...)) seen in activate.py, logout.py and resend_activation.py, with no runtime effect; reset_password.py passes url_for(...) to after_login(), which does the redirect itself, a legitimate pattern.

incidental.summary: exported values in changedetectionio/blueprint/** do not read os.environ directly
incidental.reason: Members are fixed constants (REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES, ACCESS_TOKEN_SECONDS, DEFAULT_NAME) that have no reason to be env-tunable; the outlier is an env-tunable limit written exactly the house way (float(os.getenv(...)) at module level, as in api/Changes.py, llm/client.py DEFAULT_TIMEOUT and backups/restore.py), so new tunables would be flagged for nothing. 0 of 1 counted outliers is a mistake.

legit_outliers.summary: classes in netbox/** (filtersets files) are decorated with register_filterset()
legit_outliers.reason: register_filterset (utilities/filtersets.py) keys the registry by Meta.model label, and the connection filtersets reuse ConsolePort/PowerPort/Interface, so decorating them would overwrite the primary filtersets; secondary filtersets for an already-registered model are a legitimate recurring category. Hesitated with ACCEPT since a new primary model filterset missing the decorator would be a real mistake.

legit_outliers.summary: HTTP handlers in netbox/** (api/views files) are named `*Set`
legit_outliers.reason: Router-registered ViewSets are named *ViewSet (tenancy, dcim api/views.py), but the outliers are plain APIView/RetrieveUpdateDestroyAPIView classes wired with .as_view() in ipam/api/urls.py and extras/api/urls.py; the *View suffix is correct for that recurring category, so new non-viewset API views would be falsely flagged.

legit_outliers.summary: files in saleor/graphql/app/** have a test file
legit_outliers.reason: Members with logic have direct tests (dataloaders/app.py via test_app_by_token_loader_use_cache.py, utils.py via tests/test_utils.py, app_create.py via test_app_create.py), but the only outlier thumbnail.py is two purely declarative BaseThumbnailBySizeAndFormatLoader subclasses setting context_key/model_name, exercised through the logo thumbnail queries in test_apps_installations.py; the same pattern recurs (product/dataloaders/products.py), so new declarative loader modules would get false alarms: 0 of 1 counted outliers is a mistake. Rule wording does not say how a test file is matched (clear: false).

legit_outliers.summary: Python packages use the pytest version most workspace packages use
legit_outliers.reason: Members pin "pytest>=9.0.3,<10.0.0" in their dev `test` dependency group (core, openai, text-splitters, anthropic pyproject.toml). The lone outlier, langchain-tests (libs/standard-tests/pyproject.toml:28), is a pytest plugin library that lists pytest as a published runtime dependency, and it leaves the upper bound off its other pytest-ecosystem deps as well, so downstream packages can choose their own pytest. Leaving the cap off is deliberate and would recur for any shipped test-helper package. With 0 of 1 counted outliers a mistake, the label is WRONG. No lint or CI check enforces the pin; I also weighed mixed_group as the reason, since runtime deps and dev groups are mixed in one rule.

legit_outliers.summary: exported values in src/** do not read os.environ directly
legit_outliers.reason: Every outlier is a Django setting in settings/prod.py or settings/test.py, whose job is to read os.environ (settings/base.py does the same throughout); ordinary module constants like ANSI_ESCAPE_RE or switchports/constants.py simply have no reason to. New settings would be flagged for nothing.

GetAdminCategoryPermissionsHook extends ActionHook on purpose: plugins append actions that each contribute permissions, which __call__ concatenates; ActionHook is the second hook kind in plugins/hooks.py (also used by posting/hooks/validate_posting.py), so new action hooks would get false alarms. 0 of 1.

ValidatePostingHook deliberately extends ActionHook (plugins append_action validators that all run), the second hook kind defined in plugins/hooks.py and also used in permissions/hooks/get_admin_category_permissions.py; a new action hook in posting/hooks would be falsely told to extend FilterHook. 0 of 1.

legit_outliers.summary: HTTP handlers in wger/** (api/views files) are decorated with utils.extend_schema()
legit_outliers.reason: Members are custom @action methods and plain ViewSet get() handlers whose responses drf-spectacular cannot infer (manager/nutrition api views, core ApplicationVersionView.get); the only outlier overrides the standard list() of a ReadOnlyModelViewSet with serializer_class set, so its schema is inferred automatically, and future overrides of standard actions would be false alarms. Hesitated with ACCEPT, since a new custom @action without extend_schema would be worth flagging.

Tenant-scoped models (APIToken, Tag, Backtest, RecurringCharge in models.py, all models live in this one file) carry an organization FK, but Organization is the tenant itself (one_off) and Team/TeamInviteToken are team-level models that sit above organizations and are scoped by a team FK, a recurring category that would be falsely flagged. Hesitated with ACCEPT since org scoping is the multi-tenancy boundary checked in permissions.py.

legit_outliers.summary: HTTP handlers in app/api/** call jsonify()
legit_outliers.reason: JSON endpoints return jsonify(...) (notification.py, setting.py, export_data in export.py), but export_aliases returns an importable CSV via alias_export_csv, a file-download endpoint that legitimately does not return JSON; new download endpoints would be falsely flagged.

legit_outliers.summary: HTTP handlers in changedetectionio/** are decorated with validate_openapi_request()
legit_outliers.reason: flask-restful Resource methods in api/ carry @validate_openapi_request (Search.get, Notifications.post); the only outlier Spec.get is the public, unauthenticated GET that serves the spec itself and reads no input, and the decorator skips validation for GETs anyway (api/__init__.py:259), so nothing is at stake under R3 and 0 of 1 counts. Wording 'HTTP handlers in changedetectionio/**' wrongly suggests Flask blueprint routes too, hence clear=false; hesitated with ACCEPT since new API resources taking bodies should be validated.

misdescribes.summary: functions in app/** do not use redirects to computed URLs
misdescribes.reason: Many members redirect to computed URLs without being flagged: login.py and api_to_cookie.py redirect(next_url), oidc.py/google.py redirect(authorization_url), oauth/views/authorize.py redirect(final_redirect_uri) and redirect(construct_url(...)); the rule is false for the group, and after_login is only one of many such redirects (its callers mostly sanitize next_url).

mixed_group.summary: classes in netbox/** (types files) are decorated with register_type()
mixed_group.reason: Concrete model types are decorated with @register_type(model, ...) (circuits, dcim, ipam, core), but the only outlier, NestedGroupObjectType in netbox/graphql/types.py, is an abstract base type kept for plugin compatibility alongside other base types that cannot be bound to a model; 0 of 1, so a new base type there would be wrongly flagged.

mixed_group.summary: classes in netbox/** (model_forms files) call FieldSet()
mixed_group.reason: Standard edit forms declare fieldsets of FieldSet() (CircuitForm, tenancy/vpn/wireless forms), but the outliers are plain forms.Form/ModelForm helpers (DeviceVCMembershipForm, VCMemberSelectForm, PopulateDeviceBayForm; extras BookmarkForm, SubscriptionForm, TableConfigForm, NotificationGroupForm), an inline hidden-field JournalEntryForm, or forms rendered by custom templates (DeviceForm -> dcim/device_edit.html, VLANForm -> ipam/vlan_edit.html, CableForm, VirtualChassisForm); 0 of 12 are mistakes.

mixed_group.summary: classes in netbox/** (choices files) are named `*Choices`
mixed_group.reason: ChoiceSet subclasses in app choices.py files (circuits, dcim, ipam, vpn) are named *Choices, but the scope also catches utilities/choices.py#Choice (a tuple subclass beside the ChoiceSet definition) and the form-field classes in utilities/forms/fields/choices.py; 0 of 4 counted outliers are mistakes, so a new form field there would be told to be named *Choices.

mixed_group.summary: files in saleor/graphql/order/** have a test file
mixed_group.reason: Concrete mutation modules have matching tests (order_note_add.py -> test_order_note_add.py, order_void.py -> test_order_void.py), but both outliers are shared helpers: draft_order_cleaner.py holds clean_* functions used by draft_order_create/update, and order_note_common.py is an abstract OrderNoteCommon base (Meta.abstract=True) tested through its subclasses; new helper/base modules would be flagged for nothing (0 of 2). Wording is also vague about how a test file is matched (draft_orders.py maps to test_draft_order_bulk_delete.py).

mixed_group.summary: classes in src/** (serializers files) are named `*Serializer`
mixed_group.reason: Six outliers are DRF serializer field classes (subclasses of serializers.Field/ChoiceField/FileField, named *Field), a recurring different kind of thing; only PartThumbSerializerUpdate (part/serializers.py:259) is a serializer off the naming scheme, 1 of 7.

mixed_group.summary: classes in src/** (admin files) are named `*Admin`
mixed_group.reason: Admin files also hold TabularInline classes consistently named *Inline (company, machine, plugin, stock, users), a ModelForm (InvenTreeGroupAdminForm) and a resource Meta template (GeneralExtraLineMeta); these are not ModelAdmins, so new inlines and forms would be falsely flagged.

mixed_group.summary: classes in src/** (models files) call utils.translation.gettext_lazy()
mixed_group.reason: Models use _() for verbose_name/help_text (AuditLogEntry, Company), but models files also contain managers, querysets and an enum metaclass with no user-facing strings; only Owner (users/models.py:502, a model whose fields lack translated verbose_name) is worth a look, 1 of 6.

mixed_group.summary: classes in src/** (api files) are named `*Serializer`
mixed_group.reason: Serializers in api.py files are named *Serializer (access_cards, networks, virtual), but the outliers are a serializer field (lib/mixins/api.py), DRF permission and filter-backend classes (lib/permissions/api.py) and a FilterSet (virtual/api.py): other kinds of classes that legitimately live in api.py, 0 of 5 mistakes.

Only the hook classes in permissions/hooks/ override __call__ and delegate to FilterHook/ActionHook via super().__call__(); the outliers are ordinary classes (a result object in checkutils.py, a debug-toolbar Panel, the permissions proxy, queryset filters) with no __call__ at all, so any new non-hook class in misago/permissions would be flagged for nothing. 0 of 6 counted outliers are mistakes.

Members are hook classes whose __call__ returns super().__call__(...); outliers are plain helper classes (checkutils.py result, panels.py debug panel, proxy.py, querysets.py) with no base behaviour to delegate to. 0 of 5 counted outliers are mistakes; 'call super()' without saying which method is also vague.

mixed_group.summary: classes in wger/** (serializers files) are named `*Serializer`
mixed_group.reason: Serializer classes (LanguageCheckSerializer, MealSerializer, WeightEntrySerializer, gallery ImageSerializer) are named *Serializer, but all three outliers are custom DRF field classes (subclassing ImageField/FileField/PrimaryKeyRelatedField) co-located in serializers.py and correctly named *Field; a new field class there would be falsely told to end in Serializer.

mixed_group.summary: exported values in wger/** (urls files) call urls.path()
mixed_group.reason: Pattern lists in urls files (patterns_gym_config, nutrition patterns_bmi, weight urlpatterns) are lists of path() calls, but wger/urls.py also defines the root DRF DefaultRouter (the one aggregator, one_off) and a sitemaps dict mapping names to Sitemap classes, a different kind of module-level value that has no reason to call path(); 0 of 1 counted outliers is a mistake.

mixed_group.summary: backend: classes in metering_billing/serializers/** are named `*Serializer`
mixed_group.reason: Serializers in auth/request/response_serializers.py follow *Serializer, but serializer_utils.py and model_serializers.py also hold DRF field classes (*UUIDField, SlugRelatedField*, ActivityGenericRelatedField) and a JSON encoder, which are a different kind of thing; only 2 of 23 counted outliers are misnamed serializers, so a new field class would be told to be named *Serializer.

mixed_group.summary: backend: exported values in app/integrations/** call get_logger()
mixed_group.reason: Members are the module-level `logger = get_logger(__name__)` lines (celery/core.py, sentry.py, periodic_sync_task.py); the outliers at backfill_task.py:510-511 are backwards-compatibility aliases of a task, a different kind of exported value that would be told to call get_logger().

mixed_group.summary: backend: classes in app/repositories/** are named `*Repository`
mixed_group.reason: WriteCounts (data_point_series_repository.py:144) is an int-subclass result type returned by bulk upserts, not a repository; the repositories package routinely co-locates such value types (NamedTuples, dataclasses like SourceRanking, SampleDay), so 0 of 1 counted outliers is a mistake.

DTOs in application_dto.py and project_dto.py extend pydantic BaseModel, but the one outlier, ExtendedStringType in validator_dto.py, is a str subclass field type, not a DTO; 0 of 1 counted, so a helper type added under dtos/ would be flagged wrongly.

Forms in dashboard views do extend FlaskForm (mailbox.py, alias_trash.py), but AliasLog in alias_log.py is a view-model data holder, like the Stats and ContactInfo dataclasses in index.py and alias_contact_manager.py; a new such helper class would be told to extend FlaskForm.
